# Render vs real — LROC NAC, dev (training) split pilot

**SOURCE-BASED · UNVALIDATED · dev split only.** These are not the held-out headline numbers of the pre-registered protocol; the §8 claim rule cannot be applied to them. Generated by `python -m tools.validation.render_vs_real.report` (session R4, 16–17 Nov 2026). Protocol `docs/v2/RENDER_VS_REAL_PROTOCOL.md` (frozen) + amendments A1–A4 (hashes in `docs/v2/PREREGISTRATION.md`, registered before any score). Plan `docs/v2/PHASE_5_R4_PLAN.md`.

**Held-out run:** the pre-registered held-out LROC NAC run (Amendment A5, 17 Nov 2026) is reported in `docs/validation/RENDER_VS_REAL_HELDOUT.md`. The §8 claim rule is applied there, not here. LROC WAC 643 nm: dev pilot `RENDER_VS_REAL_WAC_DEV.md` (A6) and held-out run
`RENDER_VS_REAL_WAC_HELDOUT.md` (A7).

Imagery: LROC NAC CDR, NASA PDS (public domain per the LROC terms, https://lroc.im-ldi.com/about/terms). Credit: **NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University**. SPICE: NAIF PDS `lro-l-spice-6-v1.0`. Terrain: LOLA (PGDA 78, PGDA 90, PDS LDEM).

## 1. What was scored

- Selection: 204 dev NAC images / 209 image × site rows from 16 NAIF spacecraft-CK windows (cluster sampling by download cost, A1.1), out of 495 eligible dev images (522 rows).
- Geometry: 188 rows OK, 21 gated, 0 failed (reasons in §9).
- Scored (PGDA 78, Hapke, registered) on the LOLA/LRO RS GRGM900C orbit (A4): **181 rows** — the headline set below; 7 more rows have only the FDF orbit (July 2009, before GRGM900C coverage) and are reported separately (§6.3); render/score failures: 0.
- Analysis-window pixels (PGDA 78, registered, binned ≈ 5 m): 204,922,829.

Strata of the scored rows vs all eligible dev rows (A1.1 cluster sampling is not stratified):

- **site**: site01_roi6 86/142, site04_roi3 54/140, site07_roi1 40/134, site11_roi4 1/106
- **el_bin**: el<-0.5 67/229, el>=2.5 0/4, el[-0.5,0.5) 30/119, el[0.5,1.5) 46/98, el[1.5,2.5) 38/72
- **az_bin**: E 2/57, N 14/58, NE 2/60, NW 24/71, S 40/74, SE 19/69, SW 31/60, W 49/73
- **em_bin**: em>=30 0/44, em[0,5) 180/472, em[15,30) 1/6

## 6. Registration (PGDA 78, Hapke; search ± 3 × 20 m, A4)

- Offset magnitude (m): median 23.4, P90 37.2, max 69.7; rows at the search bound: 0; beyond 60 m: 1; NCC registered median 0.666 vs unregistered 0.525.
- Ground offset split (real − render, m): along the Sun azimuth median -10.5 (P10 -33.0, P90 11.0); across it median -0.8 (P10 -20.0, P90 18.6). An along-Sun bias would mean registration is absorbing shadow-length differences (terrain), not pointing.
- Reading: for an unbiased error of σ = 20 m per axis (the documented NAC value), the offset magnitude would follow a Rayleigh law with median 23.5 m and P90 42.9 m, so the magnitudes match the documented accuracy. The along-Sun component is not unbiased, though: its median is negative at every site (site01_roi6 -24.7 (n = 86); site04_roi3 -7.8 (n = 54); site07_roi1 -16.7 (n = 40); site11_roi4 -31.3 (n = 1)). **Its cause is not determined.** Two candidates: (a) an along-track timing or orbit offset that correlates with the Sun azimuth, because polar NAC images are taken from a near-polar orbit at similar local times; (b) systematic shadow-length differences that the registration absorbs. The unregistered signed edge error (median 0.0 m, IQR -1.9…1.5 m) does not show a shadow-length bias, but it is not a direct test. Open item.
- Weak-bimodality rows: 1 (shadow IoU median 0.993); render median zero (A1.4 fallback): 118 of 181.

**Post-hoc diagnostic (not pre-registered; does not replace §3).** 15 of the 19 worst-decile rows are windows the render predicts as ≥ 98 % shadow. In the gallery above, the real windows are also almost entirely shadow, lit only on small rims or crater walls that the render places in the same spots. The darkness is filled with scattered light, a cross-track gradient and the NAC readout pattern. With so few lit pixels, the protocol's fixed Otsu rule (§2.2) puts its threshold inside the shadow's brightness distribution, and the A1 weak-bimodality test does not flag these rows. Their low IoU therefore measures the observed-mask rule on near-total-shadow windows, not a terrain or geometry miss. Over all headline rows: predicted shadow ≥ 98 %: n = 21, shadow IoU median 0.532; the rest: n = 160, median 0.949. A mask rule for such windows would have to be registered as an amendment before any held-out run; none is applied here.


## 8. Site04 RoI 3 hero point (site centre −89.78012°, −156.32023°)

55 scored dev rows of Site04 RoI 3; the hero point lies inside the imaged strip in **32** of them (the other 23 images cover part of the 10 km square but not its centre: M123104997RC, M123159272LC, M139831449RC, M139858589LC, M139878946RC, M139885744RC, M139892540RC, M139973949LC, M140883298RC, M141046118LC, M141073264RC, M142226765LC, M142240314RC, M142253882RC, M146833333LC, M146907909LC, M146935010RC, M157830228LC, M162478694LC, M162485477LC, M162492261LC, M162499044LC, M162505828LC). The pixel is the camera-model projection of the site centre at its PGDA 78 height; observed class = the protocol Otsu rule on that image; predicted = the PGDA 78 shadow pass after registration. Agreement at the point: **23/32** (observed shadow & predicted lit: 8; observed lit & predicted shadow: 1). One pixel per image, ≈ 5 m binned; a descriptive check, not a validation of the point.

Of the 9 disagreements, 8 have a predicted shadow edge within 20 m (≈ 4 binned pixels) of the point, i.e. the point sits on a shadow boundary and the miss is an edge-position error of the size reported in §3. Distances are to the nearest pixel of the other class within ± 40 binned pixels ("—" = none).

## 10. Limits (stated, not hidden)

- **Dev split only**, cluster-sampled by SPICE download cost; strata coverage in §1. Held-out images were not fetched,
  rendered or scored (guard + test). These numbers cannot be used for the §8 claim rule.
- **Binned to ≈ 5 m** (A1.3), so sub-5 m shadow detail in the NAC images is averaged away; edge errors are in metres of the
  binned grid. Only the lines crossing each site square are scored.
- **Render physics:** Cycles path tracing with a Hapke regolith of uniform 60–70° S parameters (no albedo map at the pole),
  4 bounces, 32 samples, no earthshine, no instrument PSF / stray light / noise model. Real NAC images of shadowed ground show
  scattered and stray light that the render does not reproduce; this lowers SSIM and raises the histogram distance in shadow,
  and is a property of the twin, not of the terrain.
- **Camera:** ISIS model re-implemented here (timing, detector, distortion) with NAIF CK/SPK; not run through ISIS itself.
  The registration absorbs a constant pointing error only (no rotation/scale).
- **Observed mask** is the protocol's fixed Otsu rule on the image's log I/F; where the window is almost all shadow or all lit
  (weak bimodality) it splits noise, and the IoU then measures that.
- No terrain was tuned; no photometric parameter was fitted. Products not in hand (Kaguya TC DTM, GSFC SfS, NAC DTMs) are not
  compared; SLDEM2015 does not reach these latitudes.
